chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Ishaq al-Jurjani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has appointed for the one to whom He grants authority a term and a duration of nights, days, years, and months. So if they are just among the people, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commands the Master of the Orbits to slow its revolution, so their days, nights, years, and months are prolonged. And if they are tyrannical among the people and do not act justly, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, commands the Master of the Orbits to hasten its revolution, so their nights, days, years, and months are shortened. And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has fulfilled for them the exact number of nights and months.

key_terms.صَاحِبَ الْفَلَكِ: The Master of the Orbits (referring to the celestial sphere/moon governing time)

ai.seo_question: How does divine justice affect the duration of a ruler's reign according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the metaphysical mechanism of 'tadqil' (slowing down) and 'taqsir' (speeding up) time, linking the cosmic order to political justice. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that divine justice is not merely retributive but also preservative, ensuring that rulers experience the full measure of their allotted lifespan regardless of whether their reign is extended or curtailed by their conduct.
